current_example.problem:
The table below gives the values of $\Phi^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p,$ where $p = \Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. Find the value of $z$ such that $P(Z \leq z) = 0.20.$

| $\quad p \quad$ | $0.65$ | $0.70$ | $0.75$ | $0.80$ | $0.85$ | $0.90$ | $0.95$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\Phi^{-1}(p)$ | $\,0.3853\,$ | $\,0.5244\,$ | $\,0.6745\,$ | $\,0.8416\,$ | $\,1.0364\,$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ |
current_example.worked_solution:
From the table, notice that

$$
P(Z\leq 0.8416 ) = 0.80.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
P(Z\geq 0.8416 ) = 1 - 0.80 = 0.20.
$$

By the symmetry of the standard normal distribution, we have

$$
\Phi(-0.8416) = 0.20.
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14263990/assets/2be6ef2420c8789a0ff94f4f9540533af4134690ebe0c04c50eb02f358dfa266.png)

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.8416) & =0.20 \\ P(Z\le -0.8416) & =0.20.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the required value of $z$ is $-0.8416.$
